name: Nothosaurus procedural twin
provenance: Middle Triassic; approved canonical image, Tripo image-to-model body, and independently rebuilt procedural volume twin
description: A procedural comparison body built to the delivered Tripo volume and animated on the same 27-joint rig as the textured runtime model.
notes: The procedural twin preserves the accepted generated volume but does not reuse the raw Tripo mesh's vertices or faces.
It shares the runtime body's rest rig, inverse binds, sockets, and 21 named animation clips.
This paired model remains a preview until a human approves the generated body and procedural twin together.

name: Stromatolite, tall dome
modelNote: A static preview model. The shape and its pigment are an authored first pass and no canonical pose has been greenlit for this family yet, so the silhouette may still change.
provenance: Authored library model; the gypsum flats and the conifer shore
description: A layered microbial dome, the flats' only structure. Post-extinction stromatolites grew where almost nothing else would, so this carpets the hypersaline pan where reef formers cannot live. The laminae are geometry rather than texture, with muted layer pigment carried in the vertex colours. The taller, steeper profile of the pair.
notes: Static mesh: no rig, no skin and no animation clips. Instanced scenery is drawn thousands of times and is swayed or bent by the renderer's shader rather than by bones, so a prop carries no skeleton by design.
640 triangles, one mesh, one material, vertex colours and no texture fetch.
Pivot at the base centre where the prop meets the ground; authored at the design's scale-1 size, which the game then scales per instance.
Built by tools/triassic/props/build.py from triassic-stromatolite-1.blend.
